stem: A mild symptom is found on 2 plants during the first scouting round, 6 plants in the next, and 12 plants in the third. What is most important about this result?
choices: Severity is mild, so no trend exists
The increasing incidence shows expansion over time and supports escalation
Only the first round should be recorded
The symptom proves a nutrient problem
rationale: Repeated incidence data show whether a problem is stable, expanding or resolving. An expanding pattern can be important even when individual severity remains mild.
